answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring every identity to lock a refundable bond that is slashed when peers prove duplicate or dishonest behavior. Trust is drawn from a shared lagoon of independent attestations: an agent only gains weight after unrelated peers verify its real work over time. A violet flag marks identities whose activity patterns diverge from honest norms, and a whisper network of cross-checks exposes clusters of correlated fakes, so each fake costs a bond plus weeks of waiting, far more than it can extract.
